concept.title: The needs-based test: a first run
concept.shortdesc: For each need and each place, did the draft help a person find a service that would suit them?

conbody.note: Every judgement here was made by a language model. No person has re-judged any of them, and the pass marks are placeholders. Read the numbers as a first measurement, not as a result.
conbody.p: The test covered 33 needs in 5 places (Bristol, Dorset, Lancashire, North Lincolnshire, Shropshire), 1,843 services judged. For each need and place a pool of candidate services was judged blind as suitable, unusable for this person (wrong eligibility) or not suitable. Two routes were measured:

ul.li: Search: is a suitable service in the top five results?
Browse: is a suitable service inside the category the need links to?

table.title: Needs-based test, search route, by how much a need matters
Needs-based test, browse route, by how much a need matters
Needs-based test, task success by place

ul.li: Task success is the share of needs, per place, where a suitable service was found by that route.
The pool is not the whole place. Miss rate and task success are measured against the suitable services the judges found, so browse success is a lower bound.
The search top results are part of the pool, so search is measured on its own home ground and flatters it. The comparison with browse is not like for like.
Random services were included as controls (14 of 330 were judged suitable); a high number would mean the judge says yes too easily.

section.title: What a release would still need
section.p: The classification is not ready to be frozen as a version 1 release. The gate lists:

ul.li: the test judgements are model-made and not enough are human-checked (0 checked, no agreement measured yet; need 100 at 0.85)
the per-criticality thresholds are placeholders, not agreed with stakeholders
19 safety-critical or important needs miss their bar in the browse lens: N-003, N-005, N-009, N-010, N-011, N-012, N-013, N-021...
